title: Requirement register: one row per line of the brief, the gate that blocks it, and the number that would clear it

state_vocabulary.MET: an artefact exists and its numbers were re-read from an official page this session, or derived from numbers that were
state_vocabulary.PARTIAL: an artefact exists but covers a fraction of the corpus, or one side of a two-sided requirement is still blank
state_vocabulary.BLOCKED: the structure exists but the decisive number cannot exist without a source that does not exist or a decision nobody has taken

gate_vocabulary.G-PRICE: no official price source exists; the NFL publishes no lines
gate_vocabulary.G-RIGHTS: the data-rights / usage decision for non-NFL sources has not been taken
gate_vocabulary.G-ROUTE: the official source route for the field does not exist or is unverified for all 32 clubs
gate_vocabulary.G-CLOCK: the evidence arrives after the fact, so it cannot be used pre-kickoff without a point-in-time store
gate_vocabulary.G-SAMPLE: the sample is below the n the rule itself sets
gate_vocabulary.G-DECISION: a policy choice only the owner can make
gate_vocabulary.G-NONE: nothing blocks it; the work is unstarted

counts.note: state counts are computed at build time and never typed

rows.text: Add a price-snapshot store that records opening and closing numbers for every market we originate
rows.artefact: 39 rows across 13 Week-10/11 games, each carrying open_value and close_value for side, total and moneyline
rows.clearing_number: every originated market carries 2 dated observations (open, close) with a source
rows.clearing_condition: 39 of 39 rows have both; 0 have an official source
rows.evidence: nfl-book/data/price_snapshots.json n_snapshots=39; nfl-market/data/market_odds_raw.json declares "official": false and provider "DraftKings, syndicated through ESPN's public odds endpoint"
rows.result: The store exists and is complete for the markets it covers. What is missing is not the store: it is an official number to put in it. Every price in the repo is third-party.

rows.text: Add a verified results feed so backtests and ROI can be computed at all
rows.artefact: 137 settled games: 32 re-read line-by-line from an official game page, 105 taken from an aggregate archive
rows.clearing_number: 137 of 137 rows re-read line-by-line against an official game page
rows.clearing_condition: currently 32 of 137 (23.4%)
rows.evidence: results_feed.json n_games=137, n_line_by_line=32, n_aggregate_only=105
rows.result: ROI can be computed for the 32 line-by-line games and for the 105 aggregate games only under an unverified assumption. This session independently confirmed 13 of the 14 Week-10 finals on two official pages each.

rows.text: Originate the side first, then the total, then the moneyline
rows.artefact: publishing order fixed to side, total, moneyline, with the reason stated
rows.clearing_number: 3 markets x 14 fixtures, published in the fixed order
rows.clearing_condition: 14 side, 14 total, 14 moneyline rows
rows.evidence: origination.json 'order' = side,total,moneyline; side/total/moneyline lists each 14 rows
rows.result: The order is enforced in data and in the page. Note the moneyline is a monotone transform of the side's margin distribution; the repo says so rather than presenting it as an independent number.

rows.text: Publish the model's fair line, the market line and the difference as separate columns
rows.artefact: own_line / market_open / market_close / difference_vs_open / difference_vs_close as five columns
rows.clearing_number: a fair line, a market line and a difference for the same market, with the market line's source
rows.clearing_condition: market columns are filled from a third-party endpoint (ESPN/DraftKings), never from the NFL
rows.evidence: columns_note in origination.json; market_source_open points at sports.core.api.espn.com
rows.result: The column split is real and correct. The market column is third-party while the page banner says 'official sources only'. That is a labelling inconsistency, not a fabrication: every row carries its class.

rows.text: Separate 'signal' from 'staking' in the leaderboard so a lucky staking run cannot mask a bad signal
rows.artefact: two independent score columns; signal metrics use no prices at all, staking uses an ASSUMED -110 price
rows.clearing_number: n >= 300 graded forecasts before any strategy is ranked as skilled
rows.clearing_condition: current walk-forward sample is 105 forecasts
rows.evidence: backtest.json price_note: 'Staking uses the ASSUMED -110 price (flag FB-02); signal metrics use no prices at all'
rows.result: The separation is implemented and the assumed price is disclosed rather than hidden. The sample is 105, well under the 300 floor the repo itself sets.

rows.text: Track the depth of the replacement, not just the fact of a replacement
rows.artefact: 3 replacement rows, each naming the expected starter, the replacement and the replacement's depth label
rows.clearing_number: a depth label for every replacement, sourced from a dated official depth page per club
rows.clearing_condition: 3 rows exist; the 32-club depth register behind them is blank
rows.evidence: depth_replacements.json rows=3; depth_register.json 32 rows all 'unverified - no official depth source (FB-07)'
rows.result: Depth depth is recorded where a replacement is recorded, but the underlying register is empty. This session confirmed club depth pages exist and parse for GB and BAL, and that Houston publishes its chart as an image.

rows.text: Compute correlations only from officially sourced numbers and publish n with each value
rows.artefact: 5 correlations computed from official final scores, each with n, r, p and a 95% CI; 4 left blank with the reason
rows.clearing_number: n published on every value; 0 values computed from a price or third-party number
rows.clearing_condition: 5 computed with n, 4 blank with a stated reason
rows.evidence: correlations.json method: 'Pearson r on official final scores/dates... No market, price or third-party number is used anywhere'; CR-01 n=137 r=-0.1607
rows.result: The discipline is real. One inconsistency: CR-01 reports n=137 for a 136-game corpus, i.e. n equals the size of the results feed rather than the settled-game count. Flagged.

rows.text: Define a demotion gate that sends a live strategy back to paper
rows.artefact: gate D1 with four firing conditions, armed, evaluated against every live strategy
rows.clearing_number: a written rule that fires without a human deciding, and a recorded evaluation
rows.clearing_condition: 0 live strategies; 0 firings; rule armed
rows.evidence: demotion_eval.json result: 'no strategy holds LIVE status; D1 is armed and would fire on any of its four conditions'
rows.result: Defined and armed. It has never fired because nothing has ever been promoted, which is the honest state, not a gap.

rows.text: Pre-register every strategy; forbid backtest numbers from ever appearing on the leaderboard
rows.artefact: 5 strategies in the catalogue; 1 pre-registration registered with a rule-file hash (PREREG-002)
rows.clearing_number: strategies in the catalogue: 5; strategies carrying a registration hash: 1
rows.clearing_condition: 5 of 5 registered before their evaluation window opens
rows.evidence: nfl-book/data/strategies.json strategies=5; nfl-collector/data/prereg.json registered={PREREG-002} only
rows.result: One of five strategies is registered. The other four are described but not frozen, so their numbers are not yet admissible on a leaderboard.

rows.text: Build the availability graph as a first-class dataset (who was expected to start, who actually did)
rows.artefact: 3 rows with the expected side filled and the actual side blank
rows.clearing_number: both sides filled for every row: an expected starter and an evidenced actual starter
rows.clearing_condition: 3 rows, 0 with actual evidence at build time
rows.evidence: availability_graph.json method: 'actual starter side is left blank because no official snap-count or Game-Book source is captured (FB-07)'
rows.result: The actual side IS available this session: the inactive list (S02) and the official Game Book PDF linked from every game centre (S10, S11) both carry it. The blank was a sourcing gap, not an impossibility.

rows.text: Do not model depth from jersey order; model it from playing time
rows.artefact: none - no snap-count or playing-time table anywhere in the tree
rows.clearing_number: an official per-player snap count, or a Game Book participation row, for every player in the model
rows.clearing_condition: S13 (player stats page) publishes no snap field; the Game Book PDF does publish participation
rows.evidence: S13 read: the stats page exposes Recent Games, Career Stats, Logs, Splits, Situational - no snap count. Game Book participation is parsed in nfl-collector for 1 fixture
rows.verify: verified against official page this session
rows.result: Playing time exists officially in exactly one place that was found: the Game Book PDF. One fixture is parsed (WAS@NYG, 109 participation rows). The route is real; the coverage is 1 of 136.

rows.text: Make the injury signal a surprise, never a level
rows.artefact: 171 rows shaped for surprise = actual - expected, with the actual side blank
rows.clearing_number: an actual availability record for every row that has an expected status
rows.clearing_condition: 171 rows; 0 with actual_status at build time
rows.evidence: injury_surprise.json method: 'Actual availability is blank without an official inactive list'
rows.result: The inactive lists now exist and were read this session for 24 clubs, so the surprise column is computable today for those clubs. The blank was stale, not structural.

rows.text: Run the 32-team roster/IR sweep before any team-level model is trusted
rows.artefact: reserve-list capture covering one month, 25 dated Reserve/Injured moves
rows.clearing_number: reserve status confirmed for 32 of 32 clubs
rows.clearing_condition: 25 moves read for November 2026 only; no club-by-club roster read
rows.evidence: S03 chunks 0-1 read completely: 25 rows, dates 11/07 to 11/16
rows.verify: verified against official page this session
rows.result: Malik Willis (MIA, 11/10) is confirmed on the reserve list, which is exactly the case the brief names: he is absent from the weekly report because he is on injured reserve, not because he is healthy.

rows.text: Add a fixture-context feature set built only from published schedule facts
rows.artefact: 13 fixture rows of published schedule facts
rows.clearing_number: context fields present for every originated fixture
rows.clearing_condition: 13 rows for the 13 originated fixtures
rows.evidence: fixture_context.json rows=13
rows.result: Present for the originated fixtures only. It has not been extended to the 136-game corpus, so it cannot yet be a backtest feature.

rows.text: Store every model output as a probability plus its inputs, not just a pick
rows.artefact: 13 model outputs carrying a probability and the inputs that produced it
rows.clearing_number: a probability and a named input set on every output row
rows.clearing_condition: 13 rows
rows.evidence: model_outputs.json rows=13
rows.result: Stored as probability plus inputs, not as a pick. This is the single strongest artefact in the tree for auditability.

rows.text: Compute and publish the 'removal of luck' panel on the site dashboard
rows.artefact: control baselines (random picks, favourites only) on the same sample as the strategies
rows.clearing_number: a control baseline beside every strategy on the same n
rows.clearing_condition: 2 baselines, n=105 each, versus a 105-forecast strategy sample
rows.evidence: control_baseline.json rows=2; random_picks n=105 accuracy 0.5619
rows.result: The panel exists. Random picks score 0.5619 against 0.6000 for the free home-team baseline, which is the number that makes the point: a strategy must beat home advantage, not a coin.

rows.text: Add a two-sided 'what would change our mind' field to every strategy entry
rows.artefact: a two-sided falsifier on every strategy row
rows.clearing_number: 5 of 5 strategies carry both a confirm and a refute condition
rows.clearing_condition: 5 strategies
rows.evidence: nfl-book/data/strategies.json strategies=5, each entry carrying its own falsifier
rows.result: Present. It is two-sided: a number that would confirm the strategy and a number that would kill it.

rows.text: Price a line ourselves and publish the residual against the market, on a schedule, from day one
rows.artefact: own line published for 14 fixtures; residual against a market price blank on every row
rows.clearing_number: dated own-line x dated market-line pairs on a fixed cadence
rows.clearing_condition: 14 own lines; 0 residuals against an official market
rows.evidence: vig_free_decomposition.json: market_value, vig, divergence all null; status 'market/vig blank - no official price source (FB-01)'
rows.result: The residual cannot be computed against an official number because no official number exists. It can be computed against a third-party one, but only after the price-data policy is decided (RQ-22).

rows.text: Turn the 136-game log into the pre-registered backtest corpus
rows.artefact: 272-game corpus with 136 settled / 136 scheduled flagged explicitly, weeks 1-9
rows.clearing_number: a registration commit hash that predates the evaluation window, plus a price policy
rows.clearing_condition: 136 settled games; 163 of 272 games carry a third-party closing price; 0 carry an official one
rows.evidence: corpus_2026.json _meta settled_games=136; price_coverage_by_season 2026 with_closing_spread=163, source nflverse
rows.result: The 136-game log is a real corpus and this session spot-checked a row against the official game page (NE 10, SEA 13 on 2026-09-09 - exact match). But its prices are nflverse, not official, and the corpus is not yet the registered corpus until a price policy exists.

rows.text: Decide the price-data policy before any backtest is published
rows.artefact: policy recorded as DEC-1 option B in the decision register: prices declined, columns stay blank
rows.clearing_number: one written policy naming: the permitted providers, the usage basis, and what may be published
rows.clearing_condition: 1 policy recorded under a standing no-manual-input instruction, flagged for post-hoc owner review as RC-08
rows.evidence: decisions.json rows=10; DEC-1 = B
rows.result: A policy WAS taken, by an agent under a no-manual-input instruction, and it is flagged for your review. That is the correct handling, but it means the answer is provisional until you accept or reverse it.

rows.text: Store every injury-hub read with its clock time and publish the delta, never the level
rows.artefact: hash-chained capture ledger: 5 sealed entries, 1 dated capture directory, clock windows recorded
rows.clearing_number: a dated capture at the cadence the brief sets (Wed, Thu, Fri, plus pre-kickoff)
rows.clearing_condition: 1 capture date (2026-11-16) on disk; cron configured for 5 windows a week
rows.evidence: ledger.json entries=5, chain_head 5e5f5b2c...; captures/ contains exactly one dated directory
rows.result: The machinery is real and sealed. The delta needs at least two distinct read dates, and there is exactly one. A delta of one capture is a level, which the brief forbids.

rows.text: Put a decision-readiness table on the landing page: one row per requirement, the gate that blocks it, the number that would clear it
rows.artefact: this register plus nfl-board/pages/readiness.html, one row per requirement line
rows.clearing_number: 100% of brief lines carry a state, a gate and a number
rows.clearing_condition: computed at build time; see the counts object on the readiness page
rows.evidence: this file
rows.verify: the page is generated from this file, so the row count cannot drift from the register
rows.result: This session's own deliverable. The gate and clearing number are the decision-useful columns; the state is the least interesting of the three.

rows.text: Transcribe the venue of every fixture from the official game centre and publish it
rows.artefact: 4 of 136 settled games carry a venue transcribed from the Game Center 'Game Info' block
rows.clearing_number: a venue for every fixture, transcribed from the game centre
rows.clearing_condition: 4 of 136 (2.9%); the other 132 are blank and flagged unread
rows.evidence: venues_official.json _meta coverage: '4 of 136 settled games read in full this session'
rows.result: The method is exactly right (read the Game Info block, never infer from a team's home city) and the coverage is 4 games. This session confirmed three of those four independently: Lumen Field (SEA), MetLife Stadium (NYG), M&T Bank Stadium (BAL).

rows.text: Publish the league's dated schedule announcement beside the live schedule page
rows.artefact: schedule-page notes for the flexible-scheduling windows (Weeks 16, 17, 18), quoted on the live page
rows.clearing_number: a dated announcement URL beside the live schedule, for each flexible window
rows.clearing_condition: the league's flexible-scheduling procedures are linked from the live schedule page; no dated announcement was read this session
rows.evidence: S04 chunk 1 publishes the Week 16/17/18 TBD rules and links https://www.nfl.com/legal/flexible-scheduling-procedures
rows.verify: verified against official page this session
rows.result: The live schedule page already carries the dated policy text and the rule link. What is missing is storing the announcement with its date, so a later change is visible as a diff.

rows.text: Use official NFL Game Books for actual starters and game-day status; do not infer depth rank or snaps
rows.artefact: 1 fixture parsed: 109 participation rows (44 starters, 48 subs, 4 DNP, 13 not active), 0 join collisions with the injury report
rows.clearing_number: Game Books parsed for every settled fixture
rows.evidence: gamebook_was_nyg_reg10.json counts.by_role and join_to_report.collisions=0
rows.result: The route is confirmed: every game centre carries 'Download Game Book (PDF)'. This session saw the link on both game pages it read. The parser works on one fixture; coverage is the gap.

rows.text: Ingest game-level results to make the ratings opponent-aware
rows.artefact: team ratings fitted on game-level results rather than season aggregates
rows.clearing_number: a rating per club fitted from that club's opponents' results
rows.clearing_condition: 32 clubs rated from 136 settled games
rows.evidence: nfl-price-snapshot/data/derived/model_ratings.json; corpus 136 settled games
rows.result: Opponent-aware ratings exist. They rest on the same 136 games and therefore on the same unverified-price question the moment a residual is computed.

rows.text: Add injury and personnel ablations instead of fixed penalties (same model, with and without the features, with uncertainty)
rows.artefact: 3 ablation designs, delta and uncertainty blank
rows.clearing_number: a measured delta with a confidence interval on a chronological holdout
rows.clearing_condition: 0 of 3 ablations run, because the availability features are not yet sourced
rows.evidence: ablations.json rows=3, each status 'not run - availability/personnel features ...'
rows.result: The design is correct - identical model, one feature group toggled, difference reported with uncertainty. It cannot run until the availability features exist, and they cannot exist until the depth route is settled (RQ-28).

rows.text: Resolve the depth-order source before building the backup-deficiency feature: (a) per-club official pages verified club by club, then (b) snap counts if an official source exists
rows.artefact: 32-club depth register, every row blank with the same reason
rows.clearing_number: a verified depth source for 32 of 32 clubs
rows.clearing_condition: 2 of 32 clubs verified this session (GB, BAL); 1 confirmed image-only (HOU); 29 unverified
rows.evidence: S07 parsed 19 offense rows; S08 parsed and shows QB Brissett/Fagnano/Slovis; S09 shows the chart published as an image with no rows
rows.verify: verified against official club pages this session
rows.result: Route (a) works for at least two clubs. The blocking fact is not the route: it is that club charts are 'Unofficial' and undated on some pages, image-only on others, and the nfl.com league-wide route returns 404. Three different publication formats is the real obstacle to 32-club coverage.

rows.text: Automate immutable multi-day availability snapshots (daily, retained hashes, replayable)
rows.artefact: hash-chain ledger with sha256 per capture, CI cron for Wed/Thu/Fri/Sun/Mon, raw HTML excluded by policy
rows.clearing_number: distinct capture dates at the stated cadence
rows.clearing_condition: 1 distinct date on disk; 5 sealed entries
rows.evidence: ledger.json entries=5; captures/ has one dated directory; .github/workflows/nfl-collector.yml crons at 17:30 UTC Wed-Fri, 15:30 Sun, 17:30 Mon
rows.result: The automation is written and the chain verifies. It has produced one date. A multi-day series requires the cron to have run, which it cannot have done from a single branch session.

rows.text: Capture official inactive lists and snap counts
rows.artefact: official inactive lists exist and were read this session for 24 clubs; snap counts do not exist officially
rows.clearing_number: inactive evidence for 32 clubs, and a playing-time measure per player
rows.clearing_condition: 24 clubs of 32 in the official article; 1 fixture of Game Book participation; 0 snap counts
rows.evidence: S02 chunks 0-1: 12 games, both clubs each, incl. every 'emergency third QB' tag
rows.verify: verified against official page this session
rows.result: The brief's premise that no active list is captured was already stale when it was written; the lists exist and are read. Snap counts do not exist on any official page tested - the Game Book participation table is the nearest official substitute.

rows.text: Fix the two depth-parsing failures before widening coverage (Texans image; Packers jersey-number prefixes)
rows.artefact: GB chart now parses: the jersey prefix is '9 Christian Watson', strippable, with the raw string retained; HOU is confirmed image-only
rows.clearing_number: both failures classified by cause, with a route named for each
rows.clearing_condition: GB: parsed with number stripping. HOU: needs an authorised structured source, not transcription by eye
rows.evidence: S07 table rows all carry 'NN Player Name'; S09 has no table at all, only an image node
rows.verify: verified against official club pages this session
rows.result: Correct on both counts, and confirmed independently this session. Note the deeper problem the brief does not mention: GB's chart is dated 'Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026', so even a perfect parse is a week stale on the day it is read.

rows.text: Model depth slots as groups, not a single starter (149 club/unit/position slots list more than one rank-1 player)
rows.artefact: depth rows carry rank1/rank2/rank3 cells rather than a 'starter' column, so a group can be represented
rows.clearing_number: every multi-rank-1 slot recorded as a group with all its members
rows.clearing_condition: the register is blank, so the 149-slot claim cannot be checked against any committed artefact
rows.evidence: depth_register.json schema rank1/rank2/rank3, all blank; GB WR row lists one rank-1 and one rank-2, and GB S has the same player (Kitan Oladapo) at rank 2 in two slots
rows.verify: verified in repo and against S07 this session
rows.result: The data shape is right. Note a real case of the group problem in GB: Kitan Oladapo is the rank-2 safety in BOTH safety slots, so a naive 'rank 2 = backup' reading double-counts him. BAL RB also lists Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali behind Henry, and BAL K is an entirely empty slot.

rows.text: Treat roster turnover as a first-class data event (version depth/availability against the last official roster event)
rows.artefact: trades and reserve-list captures joined to the injury report, with conflict flags
rows.clearing_number: a roster-event version on every depth and availability row
rows.clearing_condition: reserve moves read for one month; 1 conflict join computed
rows.evidence: captures include league_transactions_trades_2026-11.json and league_reserve_list_2026-11.json; derived/conflicts.json exists
rows.result: Partly built. The brief's Illinois example (two starting-receiver trades in one article) is the right test case; the repo has the trade capture but not a version stamp on depth rows.

rows.text: Start with a singles-only shadow baseline (pre-register, freeze versions, record forecasts before kickoff)
rows.artefact: PREREG-002 registered with a rule-file sha256 as the registration, evaluated only on weeks >= 11
rows.clearing_number: a registration hash written before the evaluation window opens, and 0 results from that window used in the calibration
rows.clearing_condition: registered; evaluation PENDING; calibration reproduces the published weeks 3-10 backtest exactly (n=104)
rows.evidence: prereg.json registered.PREREG-002; eval_mcnemar.py calibration n=104
rows.result: This is the one artefact that meets the pre-registration standard fully: the commit hash IS the registration, and the evaluation is empty by construction.

rows.text: Keep parlays and prop combos behind a joint-evidence gate (a combo may only be ranked with a directly validated joint probability and the operator's void/push rules)
rows.artefact: 3 combo rows, each with leg correlation computed and joint probability / void-push rules blank
rows.clearing_number: a directly validated joint probability AND the operator's void/push rules
rows.clearing_condition: 0 of 3 combos have either; leg correlation is available (r=-0.0397 for JE-01)
rows.evidence: joint_evidence.json rows=3
rows.result: Correctly gated. The leg correlation is real and near zero for a cross-game 2-leg, which is the one case where multiplying marginals is nearly defensible - and it is still not allowed, which is the right call.

rows.text: Use proper-score leaderboard divisions (singles, game parlays, same-game parlays, prop combos), ranked by benchmark-relative skill with uncertainty
rows.artefact: 5 leaderboard rows with divisions and a benchmark-relative score; 8 gates attached
rows.clearing_number: n >= 300 and a game-cluster lower bound on the skill score
rows.clearing_condition: 105-forecast sample; 0 strategies eligible
rows.evidence: leaderboard.json rows=5; gates.json gates=8
rows.result: Divisions and benchmarks exist. Eligibility is zero, which is the correct answer at n=105 and should be the headline rather than a footnote.

rows.text: Rank with proper scores and uncertainty, not win rate (Brier skill, game-cluster lower bound, multiplicity adjustment)
rows.artefact: Brier-based ranking with a paired bootstrap and a disclosed multiplicity rule
rows.clearing_number: a lower bound that excludes 0 after the multiplicity adjustment
rows.clearing_condition: published example: Brier 0.2369 vs 0.2500 baseline, paired 95% CI on the improvement [-0.0173, 0.0416], i.e. includes 0
rows.evidence: verification/data/gates.json G2 and G8
rows.result: The method is implemented and the one published example does NOT clear it, which is why the repo claims no edge. That is the machinery working.

rows.text: Add durable snapshot storage and alerts (immutable captures outside the static site, freshness monitoring, alert on source/schema change)
rows.artefact: hash-chained ledger + a drift alarm with pre-pinned expected row counts and required fields
rows.clearing_number: captures stored outside the published tree, and an alert that fires on a schema change
rows.clearing_condition: the chain is in the git tree, not in external storage; raw bytes go to a CI artifact only (RF-18)
rows.evidence: drift_expectations.json + derived/drift_report.json; deploy artifact rule in nfl-collector.yml
rows.result: The alarm is real. The storage decision is not: captures live in the same repository that publishes the site, and the owner has not yet ruled on whether raw page content may be stored at all.

rows.text: Split the site into a public analysis layer and a private data layer (raw row-level data held privately until the terms are read)
rows.artefact: .gitignore names a private-store/ directory; no such store exists and no terms were read
rows.clearing_number: the NFL terms of use read and a written ruling on what may be republished
rows.clearing_condition: 0 terms read this session; 0 rows in a private store
rows.evidence: .gitignore line 'private-store/'; nfl-collector README holds RF-18 open
rows.result: The split is declared and not built. Every row-level dataset in this repo is currently published in the public tree, including 347 injury rows.

rows.text: Add a per-team view: starters out, replacements named, net injury count
rows.artefact: per-club injury counts and named replacements for the clubs where a replacement was found
rows.clearing_number: 3 columns for 32 clubs
rows.clearing_condition: replacement rows exist for 3 findings; injury counts exist per club; a ranking of starters-vs-backups does not
rows.evidence: depth_replacements.json rows=3; injury capture holds 347 rows across 31 clubs
rows.result: Two of the three columns exist. 'Net injury count' is not published because it needs a starter/backup split, which needs the depth route (RQ-28).

rows.text: Add an announced-starter evidence field (not an inferred replacement)
rows.artefact: an announced-starter evidence cell on the availability rows
rows.clearing_number: a dated official article naming the starter, linked per row
rows.clearing_condition: the dataset has 3 rows; official announced starters were published for at least Drew Lock (SEA) and Kyle McCord (MIA) in Week 10
rows.evidence: S01 chunk 6 news list: 'Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) has no injury designation, will start for Seahawks vs. Raiders'; 'Dolphins place QB Malik Willis on IR; Kyle McCord in line for first start'
rows.verify: verified against official page this session
rows.result: The evidence the brief asked for exists and is dated. It is published as an NFL news article linked from the injury report page, not as a structured field on any depth chart.

rows.text: Add an official depth-chart register with date and source per row
rows.artefact: 32-row register with date and source columns and every cell blank
rows.clearing_number: 32 rows, each with a date, a source URL and at least one parsed position group
rows.clearing_condition: 2 clubs verified this session; 0 rows populated in the register
rows.evidence: S07 dated 'Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026'; S08 has NO date printed on the page
rows.verify: verified against official club pages this session
rows.result: The register structure is right and the 'date' requirement is the blocker: one club dates its chart, another prints no date at all. A register row without a date is the exact lookahead leak the brief warns about.

rows.text: Calibrate what 'Questionable' means empirically instead of using old percentages
rows.artefact: designation -> play rate with confidence intervals, joined to official inactive lists
rows.clearing_number: a play rate per designation with a 95% CI, over multiple seasons
rows.clearing_condition: one season, one week: Out 70, Questionable 90, Doubtful 11 rows available; play rates not yet joined at scale
rows.evidence: committed capture: 347 rows, game_status counts {blank 176, Out 70, Questionable 90, Doubtful 11}
rows.verify: verified in repo this session; the same counts were re-derived from the live page
rows.result: The labels and the inactive lists both exist for Week 10, so a one-week calibration is computable now. A multi-season answer needs archived reports, which do not exist in the tree.
